Format Detection Histories and Covariates for Occupancy and Abundance Models

Source: R/model_matrix_input.R
model_matrix_input.Rd

Combines the output of detection_matrix() and effort_matrix() with site and observation covariates, in the exact form each modelling package expects. Sites are matched to covariates by name, never by row order, so a reordered covariate table cannot misalign them.

Two observation covariates are always added from the effort matrix:

  • effort, the camera-days in each site and occasion, for modelling detection probability as a function of effort;

  • when effort_matrix() was given split_by, one covariate per level, <split_by>_<level>, holding the share of that occasion's camera-days under the level (for example the share of effort at trail cameras).

Where no camera ran, observation covariates are NA, matching the detections.

One site covariate is always added too:

  • total_effort, each site's camera-days summed over the modelled occasions (the row sums of effort). It is in the site covariates for every output, and also in det.covs for single-season spOccupancy and spAbundance output, since those packages read detection covariates only from there.

Usage

model_matrix_input(
  detections,
  effort,
  site_covs = NULL,
  obs_covs = NULL,
  coords = NULL,
  output = c("unmarked", "spOccupancy", "spAbundance", "array"),
  seasons = NULL
)

Arguments

detections

The array returned by detection_matrix() (species x site x occasion).

effort

The effort_matrix() the detections were built from.

site_covs

A data frame of site covariates, or NULL. Sites are matched by a column with the same name as the effort matrix's site_col (for example "locationID") or a site column, else by row names.

obs_covs

A named list of observation covariates, each a site x occasion matrix with the same site and occasion names as detections, or NULL. These are for covariates you build yourself, such as rainfall per occasion. effort and the <split_by>_<level> shares are always added from the effort matrix, so leave split_by columns out; a name that clashes with an automatic covariate stops the function. Use one share per split variable in a model formula, since the shares of all levels add up to 1.

coords

Site coordinates for spatial models, or NULL: a data frame with the site column and two coordinate columns (for example projected X and Y in metres), or a two-column matrix with sites as row names.

output

"unmarked" (default), "spOccupancy", "spAbundance" or "array".

seasons

A vector or NULL. For multi-season models, the season of every occasion (one value per column of detections), for example the year each occasion starts in. Needs an effort matrix built with align = "calendar", so every site's occasion k covers the same dates.

Value

The model input described for output. Stops if a site in detections has no row in site_covs or coords, if obs_covs do not match the detections, or if a needed modelling package is not installed.

effort or total_effort?

Both describe sampling effort, at different resolutions:

  • effort varies by occasion, so an occasion when one of a cell's three cameras ran is not treated like one when all three ran. It is the better choice for detection probability whenever the model accepts observation covariates.

  • total_effort is one value per site. Use it in models or formulas that take site covariates only, or to compare with effort: if detection depends on total_effort but not on effort, sites differ in how much they were sampled more than occasions do.

total_effort counts only the occasions in the detections, so it leaves out the days after dur that effort_matrix() dropped. It therefore differs from cellEffort in the resampled covariates of resample_covariates_and_observations(), which counts every day each camera ran. The two give the same total only when dur keeps every day. A site_covs column named total_effort stops the function.

The outputs are:

"unmarked"

An unmarkedFrameOccu (occupancy) or unmarkedFramePCount (abundance) for one species; an unmarkedFrameOccuComm for several species with occupancy data, for unmarked::occuComm(); a named list of unmarkedFramePCount for several species with abundance data; and an unmarkedMultFrame (one species) when seasons is given, for unmarked::colext() or unmarked::pcountOpen().

"spOccupancy"

A list with y, occ.covs, det.covs and coords: y is site x occasion for one species (PGOcc(), spPGOcc()), species x site x occasion for several (msPGOcc(), sfMsPGOcc()), and gains a season dimension before the occasions when seasons is given (tPGOcc(), tMsPGOcc()).

"spAbundance"

A list with y, abund.covs, det.covs and coords, for NMix() (one species) or msNMix() (several).

"array"

Plain arrays and tables for custom models in JAGS, NIMBLE or Stan: y, effort, effort_by_unit, site_covs, obs_covs, coords, the dimensions, and observed, which is TRUE where a camera ran.

See also

effort_matrix() and detection_matrix(), which build its inputs.

Author

Zachary Amir

Examples

# one camera at each of three stations for 10 days
deps <- data.frame(
  deploymentID = c("A", "B", "C"),
  locationID = c("s1", "s2", "s3"),
  deploymentStart = as.POSIXct("2024-03-01 00:00", tz = "UTC"),
  deploymentEnd = as.POSIXct("2024-03-11 00:00", tz = "UTC"),
  baitUse = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
)
eff <- effort_matrix(deps, site_col = "locationID", w = 5, split_by = "baitUse")

# a feral pig at two stations
obs <- data.frame(
  deploymentID = c("A", "C"), eventID = c("e1", "e2"), scientificName = "Sus scrofa",
  eventStart = as.POSIXct(c("2024-03-02 03:00", "2024-03-08 21:00"), tz = "UTC")
)
y <- detection_matrix(obs, eff, "Sus scrofa")

# site covariates, deliberately in a different order to the detections
covs <- data.frame(locationID = c("s3", "s1", "s2"), elevation = c(820, 640, 700))

# plain arrays for a custom model
inp <- model_matrix_input(y, eff, site_covs = covs, output = "array")
inp$site_covs
#>    elevation total_effort
#> s1       640           10
#> s2       700           10
#> s3       820           10
names(inp$obs_covs)
#> [1] "effort"        "baitUse_FALSE" "baitUse_TRUE" 

# an unmarked occupancy frame
if (requireNamespace("unmarked", quietly = TRUE)) {
  umf <- model_matrix_input(y, eff, site_covs = covs, output = "unmarked")
  umf
}
#> Data frame representation of unmarkedFrame object.
#>    y.1 y.2 elevation total_effort effort.1 effort.2 baitUse_FALSE.1
#> s1   1   0       640           10        5        5               0
#> s2   0   0       700           10        5        5               1
#> s3   0   1       820           10        5        5               0
#>    baitUse_FALSE.2 baitUse_TRUE.1 baitUse_TRUE.2
#> s1               0              1              1
#> s2               1              0              0
#> s3               0              1              1
